encounter.text: A small mouse — young, barely past kit-age — is huddled against a wet wall, clutching a piece of string tied into a bracelet. They look up when they hear you, ears flat, eyes bright with held-back tears. 'I went too far,' they say. 'I can't find the way back up.'

choices.text: Take the time to guide them back toward the surface.
Give them a kind word and point the way.
You don't have time. Walk on.

guided.text: It takes a while. The kit talks the whole way — about their mother, their three brothers, a rat named Pip who once stole their lunch. By the time you see the light from the upper grates, a guard rat is waiting with frantic eyes. She presses coins into your hand before you can speak, already kneeling in front of the kit.

pointed.text: The kit looks at where you're pointing, then back at you. 'That way?' 'That way.' They take a deep breath, clutch their string bracelet, and scurry off without looking back. You watch until they're out of sight. Something in your chest feels easier.
